Facebook might soon need to add "Just got served divorce papers" to its list of relationship statuses. A judge in New York has ruled that using Facebook is a valid way for a woman in Brooklyn to serve her husband with divorce papers.

Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband for several years. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they have been unable to find Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku to deliver the papers. Court documents show that Baidoo can reach her husband by phone, but he says he has no fixed address and no job.

This story sounds like a science fiction movie. A person has a terrible accident, ends up in the hospital, and is brain dead while on life support. Doctors usually ask the family to donate organs to save up to eight people. But in this case, the family is asked to donate the entire head to save just one person. This might be someone who is paralyzed from the neck down but has a healthy mind. Although this idea seems crazy, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are close to making it happen. He calls this project "HEAVEN," which stands for "Head Anastomosis Venture." "Anastomosis" means surgically connecting two parts.

Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending, but police say his story ended in tragedy on Tuesday. The teenager, who had received a heart transplant, stole a car, broke into a house, shot at an elderly woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and then died when his car crashed into a pole.

In 2013, Stokes’ family told the media that an Atlanta hospital refused to give him a heart transplant. The hospital said this was because Stokes had a history of not following medical instructions. At that time, Mark Bell spoke for the Stokes family.

At Garissa University College in Kenya, the sun had not yet risen. Most students were sleeping in their beds, but a few had already woken up to attend early morning Christian prayers.

The attack began around 5:30 a.m. on Thursday (10:30 p.m. ET on Wednesday). It started with an explosion and gunshots at the front gates of the school. The attackers continued shooting as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross reported that they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took hostages, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, a 25-year-old man, died in police custody 15 days ago. He was arrested for a weapons charge and suffered a severe spinal cord injury, which caused his death. His death has caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department.

A white casket was placed at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor him. Gray’s death is part of a series of high-profile cases involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many people have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral included civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of other people who died in police custody.

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I didn’t start fighting for food policy until much later. In 2007, my wife mentored a young girl who was searching through trash just to find something to eat. This experience inspired me to start Food Policy Action and get involved in political issues about food, including hunger and factory farms. I haven’t worked alone on this. A major influence was "The Meatrix," a 2003 animated video that parodied "The Matrix." Produced by the GRACE Communications Foundation, it highlighted the health risks and environmental damage caused by factory farming.

Dan Swangard is a doctor who has seen many patients die. He has watched people pass away in hospitals while receiving pain medication, and he has seen families struggle with fear as death takes weeks or months. Now, this topic is personal for him. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that had spread. Doctors removed parts of his pancreas and liver, along with his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48 years old, knows the cancer is likely to come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The special forces were on the ground but did not fight directly. Instead, they helped organize and guide the battle against Houthi forces and fighters who support former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also helped drop weapons and communication equipment by parachute. Meanwhile, the Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important areas in the southern port city of Aden after strong Saudi airstrikes. This move was a change from the day before, when the Houthis had taken control of the presidential palace.

A mother from Detroit was arrested last month after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer. This week, she was charged with murder and torture.

The prosecutor, Kym Worthy, says Mitchelle Angela Blair killed her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

Detroit Police Chief James Craig said the bodies were found wrapped in plastic inside the freezer on March 24. A court worker was doing an eviction at the house when they made the discovery.

An expert who examines bodies has determined that Stoni died from being hit by blunt objects, and Stephen died from being hit by blunt objects and from heat injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the current world heavyweight boxing champion, is preparing for an important fight. However, he is mostly thinking about the political situation in his home country, Ukraine. He spoke to CNN from his training center in Miami before his match with American boxer Bryant Jennings, which will take place in New York on April 25. Klitschko said he is shocked and upset by the crisis in Ukraine. He explained that Ukraine is suffering because of a war with Russia. He clarified that Ukraine did not attack Russia; instead, Russia is the one causing the conflict.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made small references to his famous roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman." In his opening speech, he noted that much has changed since he first hosted the show in 1982. He mentioned that he has a 31-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend. Fans who wanted to see him fully act out his famous characters were disappointed. The SNL cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song asking Keaton to play Batman and Beetlejuice with them. He only responded with a few short jokes.

About a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell, waiting to attack. He then beat up a guard who was checking the jail. Taylor took the guard’s uniform and keys. He walked out of the jail and got into the guard’s 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old was supposed to be sentenced in May. No one knows where he is now. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m.

A New York City detective, Ian Cyrus, has been suspended. He is accused of stealing $3,000 during an illegal raid on cigarettes. Police spokesman Stephen Davis confirmed this.

Video from a local news station shows Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving a store called Yemen Deli and Grocery in Brooklyn. This happened last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes.

The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. He thought one of his employees had taken it. But when he checked the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw.

This event, which will likely be called the Hatton Garden heist, was a terrible scenario for people who store valuables in safe deposit boxes, but it would be a perfect plot for a movie. Thieves used heavy cutting tools and climbing gear to break into the vault of a well-known safe deposit company in central London. They did this during the recent holiday weekend, possibly using up to four days to search through many safe deposit boxes. They reportedly stole hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of jewelry and cash. One former police official estimates they may have stolen as much as 200 million pounds, or about $300 million.

As we get closer to April 27, the day South Africa celebrates the first elections after apartheid in 1994, we are seeing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are angry about this violence, and they are speaking out loudly on social media using the hashtag "#WeAreAfrica" to show that everyone needs to stand together against this injustice. These repeated attacks on migrants and their belongings suggest that South Africa’s dream of being a "rainbow nation" is failing. That dream was not just about having people of many different ethnicities living together, but also about everyone having the dignity to live well, regardless of their race or social class.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, agreed to stop fighting with Iraq. He later said he felt like he was "drinking poison" because he had to accept this peace deal. The war had been very important for his government, the Islamic Republic, which he started in 1979, just before Iraq attacked Iran. Khomeini got both his supporters and his critics to fight against Iraq. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Iraq wanted to stop fighting earlier. This long war helped make his government stronger. When the war finally ended, Iran’s economy was in bad shape, and the volunteers who had fought hard were no longer visible.

The concept of sustainable development suggests that unchecked capitalism is too powerful and harmful. The global economy is growing very fast, doubling in size every generation. However, because Earth has limited resources and the population is increasing by one billion people every 15 years, this rapid growth is damaging the natural environment and the social systems that help people live well. Sustainable development provides a solution to this growing problem. The truth is that unchecked capitalism is driven by greed.

The United States benefits greatly from being a country that can send things into space. This ability helps protect our national security, defense, and economy. To fight current and future conflicts, combat terrorism, and handle growing threats around the world, our military relies on space tools like intelligence, GPS, and communication satellites. However, as global threats increase and the need for reliable space access grows, the U.S. faces a serious problem: we depend too much on Russian technology to meet our national security needs.

One year after nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai sent an open letter to them on Monday. Malala is a 17-year-old who won the Nobel Peace Prize. She survived an attack by the Taliban in Pakistan because they did not want her to blog about the importance of girls going to school. In her letter, she says that, like the kidnapped girls, she was targeted by militants who opposed education. She urges the Nigerian government and the rest of the world to do more to rescue the girls. This message comes shortly after Nigeria held an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers were sent to stop deadly attacks against immigrants. Their first mission was in Jeppestown, a neighborhood in Johannesburg where the violence started on Friday. While the soldiers guarded the area, police raided a hostel there. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula announced that the government would send an unknown number of soldiers to places where police are stretched too thin trying to stop the attacks. She said this move does not mean the police are failing.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards were killed in fighting with militants near the border with Pakistan. The clashes happened on Monday in the southeastern town of Negur. Iranian forces killed three of the militants during the fight.

The news agency IRNA quoted Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province. He said the militants came into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to capture the remaining attackers.

Island travelers should pay attention: Providenciales, located in the Turks and Caicos, is now TripAdvisor’s number one island in the world. Last year, it was ranked second. This year, it moved up to first place, replacing Ambergris Caye, which is an island in Belize. Ambergris Caye had been the top island for two years, but it fell out of the top ten this year. A TripAdvisor spokesperson, Julie Cassetina, said it is difficult to explain why winners change each year because the rankings depend on feedback from travelers.

The "Star Wars" story continues to grow. At a fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, the details for the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were shared. Director Gareth Edwards showed a short preview clip and explained the plot. Disney calls this movie an "anthology" rather than a "spinoff." It stars Felicity Jones. The story happens between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" (the original 1977 film). A group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal plans for the Death Star. Jones plays one of these rebel soldiers.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the historic decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and China—to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" means that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a great one. Although some strict politicians may try to complain that the preliminary agreement isn't what they wanted, for many people, it shows excellent progress, which is what they desire.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) – At 11:45 p.m. Eastern Time, we learned that two Black residents, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means that three of the six council members are now Black.

Earlier, at 6:52 p.m. Eastern Time, we reported that the weather was bad, with dark skies and radio warnings about flash floods. Despite the rain, the city opened its voting stations at 6 a.m. for local elections. Usually, very few people vote in these elections, but today was different. This was the first city election since white police officer Darren Wilson shot and killed unarmed Black teenager Michael Brown last August. Since then, this St.

On Wednesday night, a man was killed and another person was injured in a suspected terrorist attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. According to Israel Police spokesman Micky Rosenfeld, a 37-year-old Arab driver from East Jerusalem hit two people who were waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. One victim, 26-year-old Shalom Yohai Cherki, died at the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being investigated by the General Security Services.

Lauren Bacall, a famous actress who died in 2014, has put her large art collection up for sale. The collection features works by some of the most important artists of the 20th century. The items were sold in New York on March 31, after being shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles.

Bacall became famous in 1944 with her first movie, "To Have And Have Not." It was during that film that she met her husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the 2015 Golden Globes, actor George Clooney honored her in his speech.

In Kiev, Ukraine, people are worried about who might be killing supporters of Ukraine’s former President, Viktor Yanukovych. This idea isn’t new, but it became more important this week because two famous people were shot and killed in the city. One was a former member of parliament who had connections to Yanukovych. The other was a journalist who supported Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former member of parliament, was shot and killed shortly after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance to his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize civil unions for same-sex couples. On Monday, President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law that allows these unions, joining several other South American countries. Bachelet said this is an important step toward treating gay and straight couples equally. The law will start working in six months. It gives legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two people of the same sex or a man and a woman. The government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

When you fly to Florida, look out the window. Whether you are visiting family, going to Disney World, or relaxing on the beach, try to get a seat by the window before you land. As you approach Miami or Orlando, you will see the Everglades below. This area shows how mistakes made by people can be expensive to fix. From the air, the swamp looks like a messy, empty space filled with dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. In fact, one researcher caught 365,000 biting insects in just one trap during a single night.

ISIS militants took control of Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. The camp had been under attack by Syrian forces for more than two years. In early April, residents woke up to find that ISIS had taken over the area after defeating other local militia groups. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS killed people in the streets. Now, ISIS controls almost all of the camp.

For a long time, China has used a system called the "Great Firewall" to stop its citizens from reading news websites from the West or other content the government dislikes. However, a study published on Friday says this is no longer enough. China has created a new tool called the "Great Cannon" and has used it to attack servers outside of China, including servers in the United States. The study’s authors note that this tool works openly and visibly. Because China is attacking other countries so clearly, it will likely anger other nations. The authors suggest that Beijing may have expected this reaction.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any proof of why the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, caused the accident. However, a spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday that Lubitz had suicidal thoughts at some point before he became a pilot.

Investigators have not found any writings or conversations where Lubitz explained his reasons or admitted to planning the crash. But medical records show that he was suicidal at one time and received therapy for it. This happened before he ever got his pilot’s license, the spokesman, Christoph Kumpa, said.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said he would not give up. At the same time, a top Saudi military official stated that weeks of airstrikes had significantly weakened the group.

Abdul-Malik al-Houthi, the rebel leader, made these remarks in a televised speech. He said his fighters would not leave the main cities or government buildings. He also told people who think the rebels will surrender that they are dreaming.

These comments came after more than three weeks of bombings by a Saudi-led coalition. The coalition’s goal is to push back the Houthis, who took over the capital city, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power.

On April 19, 1995, twenty years ago, Timothy McVeigh blew up a large truck bomb outside the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The attack killed 168 men, women, and children and hurt hundreds of others. It is still the worst act of homegrown terrorism in U.S. history.

After the bombing, the media covered the story heavily, using phrases like "attack on the heartland" and "America's lost innocence." The country was shocked by the event. People were not just focused on how big the tragedy was, but on the fact that American citizens had attacked their own government with a level of violence that had never been seen before.

If you cared deeply about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign or join a demonstration? How long could you keep going when people ignored you or did nothing?

A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were kidnapped from their school by Boko Haram militants. Millions of people around the world joined a social media campaign to ask for their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of those people. From celebrities to world leaders, many voiced their anger using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It was one of the most popular Twitter hashtags of 2014, used in more than four million tweets.

But as weeks turned into months, there was still no sign of the missing girls. The attention on the campaign faded.

Barney Frank, a retired politician, recently spoke to a full audience in Chicago. He talked about his 45 years of working in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while holding office. He also criticized politicians who hide their sexual orientation but vote against gay rights. When a person in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about it. He told the young man not to worry about crazy people.

A violent attack at Garissa University College in Kenya killed nearly 150 people, including students, and injured dozens more. On Thursday morning, gunmen entered the campus during prayers, shooting randomly and taking hostages before security forces killed them. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi stated that the terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack. This incident happened just months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a Kenyan quarry. The group has been responsible for many attacks in the area and has also recruited some Americans, especially Somali-Americans living in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa has taken down a statue of a British colonial leader, Cecil Rhodes, after weeks of student protests. Students used social media and the hashtag #RhodesMustFall to argue that Rhodes’ history is racist. The campaign began last month, and four weeks later, the statue has been removed, so the hashtag is now #RhodesHasFallen. On Wednesday, the University of Cape Town announced that officials gave permission to take the statue down. The university stated that this was done to keep the statue safe while deciding what to do with it in the future.

Syria is becoming increasingly dangerous and deadly. According to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, 310,000 people have died since the civil war started. This number has doubled in just one year. A year ago, the death toll was 162,402, and two years ago, the United Nations reported 70,000 deaths.

The violence has caused extreme poverty for more than half of Syria’s population. These people desperately need help to survive. However, the United Nations says that food supplies are being reduced because there is not enough money or donations to support them.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly and seemed shy. However, prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten someone she saw as a rival.

According to a legal document, Tsarnaeva called a woman this summer and told her to stay away from her boyfriend. She said, "Leave my man alone" and "Stop looking for him." She also warned, "I know people who can put a bomb where you live."

Because of who she is, prosecutors did not think this was a joke. They charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies.

When she left court last December, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

Police in Gaza took a door with a drawing by the famous British artist Banksy on Thursday. This happened after a disagreement about selling the door, a police official told CNN.

The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, went to a court in Gaza. He said he sold the door for only $175 because he did not know how valuable it was.

The police in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, will keep the door until a court hearing takes place. The date for this hearing has not been set yet.

Darduna said that when his home was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had lost everything. He was left with only the doorway and the door.

On Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition continued its attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen. As the coalition gained more control, many locals fled the area, and the number of casualties rose, including dozens of civilians.

Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition destroyed the Houthi air defense systems and the defenses of supporters of Yemen’s former President, Ali Abdullah Saleh. A Saudi source said that almost all of the air bases and runways are now unusable.

Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all of Yemen’s ports. The coalition allows only carefully monitored non-military medical supplies to pass through its blockade.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, criticized his own fans for booing Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a "disgrace."

Spain's coach, Vicente del Bosque, used a new lineup for the game in Amsterdam. Iniesta started on the bench and came into the game in the 76th minute. When he entered, the home fans booed and jeered at him.

The Netherlands won the game thanks to goals from Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen in the first half. However, Hiddink was unhappy with how Iniesta was treated by the fans.

On May 21, Scotland will find out if its upcoming Euro 2016 match against Georgia will be played without any spectators. UEFA has started an investigation into the Georgian Football Federation because fans entered the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA is also looking into other charges, such as fans setting off fireworks. Additionally, they are investigating safety problems at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, including blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff failing to search fans for weapons or dangerous items.

On Wednesday, football agents were waiting to see what the new rules would be. Starting on April 1, the rules for becoming an agent will change. Now, anyone can become an agent if they pay £500 for the first year. After that, the Football Association (FA) will charge £250 each year to renew the license. Agents who already had licenses do not need to change anything. The FA plans to put a link on their website so agents can register, but as of 1pm, that link was not yet available. Mel Stein believes these new rules will cause chaos. These changes happen because FIFA has stopped controlling how agents are managed.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, has not received his salary for three months since he joined the club in January. Because of this financial trouble, he has had to ask his parents to send him money to pay his rent. Despite these money problems, Uvarenko likes the club’s fans, who he says are unique and very passionate. He told local media that the lack of money is the biggest problem he has faced at CSKA.

David Moore, 25, got very angry after leaving his home. He was stuck in heavy traffic on a busy street. Right in front of him was Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire.

Moore punched Cegielka and then broke his car with a hockey stick. This happened in front of young children. The court heard that Moore was having a bad day and lost his temper.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This loss reminded people of Spain’s bad performance in the 2014 World Cup. However, Gerard Pique says coach Vicente del Bosque should not worry too much about losing three friendly games in a row.

Holland scored two goals early in the game at the Amsterdam Arena. They kept their lead even though Spain tried hard to score in the second half. This win was important because Holland had beaten Spain 5-1 during the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. That earlier loss ended Spain’s six-year period of being the best team in the world.

Police say a mother from New York City, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany. A court order forbids Berger from leaving the country with the child. However, police believe that on March 22, the day after Kaia was dropped off for a weekend visit, they flew to Europe.

Police are searching for both of them. They were last seen at Berger’s home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21, when Kaia’s father dropped her off.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The fire produced strong flames and thick, unpleasant smoke. It destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches, looking like a scene from a disaster movie. This happened after several days of storms in Britain, which knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water ran off the slope. Fire investigators confirmed that the fire was started on purpose. They found that three separate areas of heath were destroyed: one half a hectare, one one hectare, and one 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services received 600 calls every hour across Britain as people celebrated the New Year in 2012. Paramedics were overwhelmed, and in Cambridge, a military field hospital was opened to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service reported that at the busiest time, they handled more than 600 calls per hour, which is more than three times the usual number. In Manchester, one man collapsed on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two people walked past eating late-night food. In another part of Manchester, a man was slumped in a doorway while two women walked by during their New Year celebrations.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says his mental strength helped him bounce back after being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers removed him indefinitely because of poor performance, but Mignolet returned quickly when another player, Brad Jones, injured his thigh. The 27-year-old Belgian goalkeeper explained that he stayed positive despite the disappointment of being cut from the squad. He told FourFourTwo, "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell in the Southern United States. People rushed outside to film the unusual weather.

Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded video of the ice balls hitting his backyard and splashing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hailstones falling quickly and breaking when they hit the ground.

Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard ice did not melt quickly. Within seconds, the patio was covered in white hail.

Nine crew members from a replica pirate ship called the *Liana's Ransom* had to leave their vessel because it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine. The Coast Guard rescued them using lifeboats on Tuesday. The ship was left floating 30 miles east of Portland. Officials said the ship’s engines stopped working around 12:35 a.m. on Monday, and the sails got tangled around the mast.

Beautiful photos show blue glowing algae lighting up Australia’s east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, showing a bright neon glow on one of Australia’s popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson called the sight a “beautiful supernatural scene” caused by millions of tiny plankton emitting light. A similar event happened at Sydney’s Manly Beach in August 2014. At that time, an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia that there was no need to worry about the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was rescued by zoo security after he jumped into a lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he would kill them. Later, he explained that he was drunk and believed he had a good chance of fighting the animals.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling from a fifth-story window. He landed on a car parked below the building. His father said the boy probably fell while sleepwalking. The event happened last Saturday. A hotel receptionist across the street heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car accident.

Drew Miller, a player for the Detroit Red Wings, is excited to return to the ice. This comes just one day after he received a serious cut to his face that could have blinded him. Miller said he feels very lucky that the skate did not hit his eye.

During practice on Wednesday, Miller wore a full face mask. He showed a large, bloody wound that required 50 to 60 stitches to close. The injury left a scar across his eye, but he did not lose his eyesight.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid might try to bring him back this summer. He signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July. However, he has had trouble making the left-back position his own at Chelsea. Atletico hopes this weakness gives them an advantage, but Luis stated: “I am happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until my contract finishes.”

Charlie Sumner, a 20-year-old fan of Reading Football Club, has been banned from attending matches for three years. The ban comes after he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the Madejski Stadium.

This happened last month during an FA Cup match where Reading beat Bradford City 3-0. Sumner performed the stunt while his team was already winning. He landed on his back after the flips, and stadium staff stopped him.

Sumner said going to his first game was a great experience, but he now faces a three-year ban for his actions.

A video shows a van driving near Salé, Morocco, with about six men sitting on its roof. The van was carrying football fans. As it drove fast on a busy road, it started moving side to side. Then, the van tipped over onto one side. The men on the roof were thrown off. A car following the van recorded the scary footage.

England is in Group D of the UEFA Under 17 European Championships, along with the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. The tournament takes place in Bulgaria in May.

England’s team, managed by John Peacock, is the current champion. They won last year’s final in Malta by beating Holland on penalties. To move forward to the quarter-finals in this tournament, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament is larger than before, with 16 teams instead of eight.

Also, Danny Collinge scored England’s first goal against Norway during the qualifying rounds and celebrated by running away.

An elephant was relaxing with its family near a small pool of water in South Africa’s Kruger National Park. A male buffalo came too close, which annoyed the elephant. To make the buffalo leave, the elephant sprayed water from its trunk. The spray missed the buffalo. The video shows the frustrated elephant trying to squirt the buffalo, while its young calf stays close to its parent for protection.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, has won an eight-year legal battle to clear his name. He was originally convicted in November 2006 for showing Premier League football matches on foreign TV channels at his pub, the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. The conviction was overturned because he did not have an agreement with official broadcasters. Thorpe, who is 55, says the long fight cost him heavily, including the loss of his pub.

The Irish Football Association is worried about cracks in the West Stand at Windsor Park, their stadium in Belfast. These cracks appeared overnight on Monday night. On Tuesday morning, officials closed off that area while engineers checked the damage. The association wants to make sure this problem does not stop Northern Ireland from playing their important Euro 2016 match against Romania in June.

Charlie Sumner, a 20-year-old football fan, has been banned from stadiums for three years. The ban happened because he ran onto the field topless and did four front flips during his first game at Reading’s Madejski Stadium. This happened last month during an FA Cup match between Reading and Bradford City. At the time, Reading was winning 3-0. Sumner landed on his back after each flip, and then stadium staff tackled him.

A BMW driver was arrested today after hitting and killing a student who was walking to the library. The student, Hina Shamim, was 21 years old. She died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just a few weeks before her 22nd birthday. Her BMW had five children inside.

Friends have left flowers at the place where she died. They said Hina, who was originally from Peterborough and had the nickname "Hyena," was very loved and a charming, lovely girl.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video showing them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston was posted online. The incident happened on Tuesday. The mother, whose name is not known, was reportedly angry because the student had allegedly been bullying her daughter. The video shows the mother wearing a black top on the right and the victim wearing white in the center.

Stoke City’s boss, Tony Scholes, hopes they can keep Asmir Begovic, the team’s goalkeeper, as his contract ends next year. Begovic, who plays for Bosnia, has often been linked with other teams while playing at Stoke’s stadium. Even though he has just over 12 months left on his current deal, Scholes believes they can meet the 27-year-old’s goals. Scholes told The Sentinel, “Asmir is a great goalkeeper, and we really want him to stay at the club. It’s normal to hear rumors about what happens next when you have really good players.”

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was caught reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver flipping through the pages and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. The video shows the driver looking at the newspaper while the bus is moving and when it stops at traffic lights. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says that defender Winston Reid will be ready to play in Saturday’s game against Leicester City. However, Enner Valencia will not be available.

Reid has been unable to play since he hurt his hamstring during a 1-0 loss to Chelsea on March 4. But during the international break, he returned to full training.

Valencia missed West Ham’s last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of an unusual toe injury he suffered in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not ready to play.

Five days before their wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman, who were college sweethearts, were involved in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. The crash killed Brittany and left John fighting for his life.

John survived, but his body was badly injured. Doctors told him that he would likely spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and use a wheelchair. The future looked very difficult for the 25-year-old assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College. However, against all odds, John recovered. On March 24, he helped lead his team to a championship title.

Lucas (on the left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard played in a charity game at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a Brazilian midfielder, wants to get back to his best performance level after recovering from an injury.

From late November until February, he started 16 out of 19 games. During this time, the team’s results improved significantly. However, he hurt his groin during a match against Everton in February and missed 10 games.

He did not play in the loss to Manchester United, which was Liverpool’s first league defeat since mid-December. But he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Some people find father-daughter photos boring. A Japanese photographer named Yûki Aoyama has found a fun way to make them more interesting. In his new photos, the daughters look straight at the camera and smile. Meanwhile, their fathers jump into the air and strike dramatic poses. These pictures are from Aoyama’s latest book, which is called "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old who robbed a bank in broad daylight and took £3,000 in cash. The robbery happened at 12:30 pm at a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff.

Detectives have released CCTV images of the suspect. He is a white male, 5ft 9in to 6ft tall, with greying black hair and glasses. He was wearing black clothing. No one was hurt during the robbery, and police are confident that the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco’s ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. This ban was originally put in place by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

Morocco was kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and was fined $1 million. The CAF also asked for an additional $9 million in compensation because Morocco withdrew as the host country due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. The 2017 tournament was won by Ivory Coast, which was held in Equatorial Guinea.

Now, Morocco is allowed to participate in the next two African Cup of Nations events.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he is now ready to try for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would mean Ronny Deila’s goal of keeping the young Belgian player for another year would fail. However, Boyd also sees a good side to this. He believes Denayer’s growth can serve as a great example to encourage other young talents to move to Celtic for their next career step. The 19-year-old defender has done well on loan at Celtic this season. He recently earned his first international game for Belgium in a Euro 2016 match against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England against Italy, which helped him prove his critics wrong. He said that people like Paul Merson, who doubted him, gave him the motivation he needed. This has been a difficult season for the 23-year-old, who hasn’t played as well as he did when he first started playing for the national team. However, England’s manager, Roy Hodgson, still believed in him. Townsend proved that faith by scoring an amazing goal at the Juventus Stadium in Turin. He scored England’s equalizing goal in a 1-1 friendly match against Italy on Tuesday night. After scoring, Townsend celebrated with his teammates from Tottenham Hotspur, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

The Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of the Spanish soccer team Atletico Madrid. This deal was finalized on Tuesday during a special meeting. A lawyer for Wanda Madrid Investment approved the purchase of 726,707 shares for €45 million (about £32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were required to make it official. Wanda Group’s chairman, Wang Jianlin, wants to make Atletico Madrid more popular in Asia. Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, is talking to the press.

Antonio Conte said that returning to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 tie with England brought back “very fond memories,” even though reports say he received death threats in the days before the friendly. Conte became Italy’s manager in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli, after the team failed to advance past the group stage of the World Cup last summer. However, his first seven months as head coach have been difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to save a 2-2 match against Bulgaria last Saturday. Also, Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after player Claudio Marchisio injured his knee just before the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that Hibernian (Hibs) could finish in second place, ahead of Rangers, during the last month of the season. He believes this is because the final games might be easier for Hibs.

Murray’s team, Dumbarton, has played against both Rangers and Hibs this season, and they will play them again in the final weeks. Right now, Rangers are doing well—they have beaten Hibs and Cowdenbeath. However, Hibs recently lost to Raith.

Even though Rangers are currently winning, Murray does not think they can keep up their speed for the rest of the season. He expects the advantage to shift back to Hibs soon.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit as he flew back to England. He had just finished playing for Belgium in the Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel.

Even though Mignolet was on the team list for both games, he did not play. The coach chose Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois instead. This meant Mignolet did not get to add to his 14 international appearances.

Mignolet posted the photos on his official Facebook account on Wednesday.

A large country property is for sale for £6 million. It is located on 200 acres of land near Bridgnorth, Shropshire. The estate includes a main house that is officially listed as Grade II, along with five smaller cottages. The property also has a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and its own cricket field. The main house, called Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms. It was built in 1814 and has only been sold twice since then. Because the grounds are private and secluded, the house might appeal to famous people who want privacy.

Two police officers at a college in Dallas have been suspended from their jobs. This happened after a video showed them bullying four students and arresting one of them after hitting him first. The event took place at El Centro College. A student named Charles Adams recorded the incident on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened last Wednesday. The officers approached the students, who were waiting for a bus outside the downtown campus.

Gary Locke has been made the permanent manager of Kilmarnock. He signed a three-year contract.

Locke used to manage Hearts. He joined Kilmarnock last summer as assistant manager to Allan Johnston. When Johnston left in early February, Locke took charge of the team.

Locke is 39 years old. He will speak to reporters on Friday morning. Since he started managing, his team has won six out of seven games, losing only once.

This weekend, the biggest match in German football takes place. It is called "Der Klassiker," but it is not as exciting as usual. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles together. Bayern Munich is likely to win again this season.

However, this time the two teams are far apart in the rankings. There is a 31-point difference and nine places between them. Even so, the match is still very important, just like it always is when these two clubs play each other. The photo shows Jurgen Klopp, the manager of Borussia Dortmund, celebrating with his players after they beat Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl named Deva Joseph was stuck at London Stansted airport because easyJet did not let her on her flight to Spain. The airline said she had too much hand luggage—two bags instead of one. Deva cried because she couldn’t go home. She offered to pay extra to put the second bag in the cargo hold, but the airline said they only accept credit cards. Deva does not have a credit card because she is too young.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch to the back of the head. The punch was so hard that it made a loud cracking sound. Robson was drunk after his grandfather’s funeral. He hit Potts because Potts tried to stop a fight outside a sports bar called NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear. This happened in November last year. Robson has been violent before. He was sent to prison for three and a half years.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece are two of the best feelings in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was special because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League.

In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the penalty box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood got confused and almost ran into each other. Ellen White took advantage of the mistake, spun around, and kicked the ball into the corner.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. They shout commands like "kill, stab, slash, and jab" while performing eight specific movements. The training is led by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier, at Huizhou Integrated High School on March 27. The 68 students involved are between 16 and 18 years old. For safety, the knives they use are fake, not real. School official Huang Anruo confirmed that the daggers are not real.

We spend one-third of our lives sleeping, but many people ignore what their body and mind actually need to feel refreshed every day. The Sleep Health Foundation found that 30% of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that if we miss sleep, we have to make up for it to stay functional throughout the week. On average, adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, with a healthy range of seven to nine hours.

Video has been posted online showing a fight between neighbors in a Perth suburb. The video shows an angry woman shouting racist insults at a group of men who appear to be African. She then goes into her neighbor’s front yard, holding a metal crowbar, yelling at the men, and swinging the tool at them. The men then grab their own weapons, and a fight begins. The woman is heard saying, “I don’t deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys.”

Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all trying to sign 19-year-old Valencia defender Jose Luis Gaya this summer. They want to take him away from Real Madrid. Sports reporter Pete Jenson looks at why these English clubs are interested.

Gaya has a buy-out clause of £13.5 million. This is much cheaper than what Luke Shaw, who is about the same age and has similar potential, cost (£27 million). So, it makes sense for these clubs to be interested. However, they might still worry about whether Gaya would fit well in the Premier League. The photo shows Gaya playing for Valencia against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to find a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. A 59-year-old man named Edward West allegedly pointed a gun at the teens in Salem and told them, "get ready to die." Just then, a stranger on a green motorcycle arrived. He used his helmet to knock the gun out of West's hands, allowing the teens to escape.

Tim Sherwood has told Ron Vlaar to show he is still a good player now that he is ready to return as Aston Villa’s captain. Sherwood wants Vlaar, who is now healthy, to help the struggling team finish the season strongly. He also warned that people might have forgotten how well Vlaar played in the World Cup last year.

Vlaar was a key player for Holland when they reached the semi-finals in Brazil. Even though he missed a penalty in the shootout against Argentina, his performance led to interest from Manchester United.

Aston Villa will welcome back their captain, Ron Vlaar, when they play at Old Trafford on Saturday. The strong Dutch defender is returning from injury to help the team fight against being relegated.

Tim Sherwood, the manager of Aston Villa, says he is not worried about the club being sold this summer. He wants to create a team that fits his style for next season, as long as the club stays in the league. It is known that the current owner, Randy Lerner, is talking with a potential buyer. If someone else buys the club, people might question whether Sherwood will keep his job. However, Sherwood is focused on keeping the team in the league first. After that, he plans to use the summer break to make long-term changes. Sherwood insists he is not concerned about the takeover talks. Christian Benteke scored a goal when Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic wants Manchester City to let Jason Denayer come back for another loan next season. However, City has said that their young players from the Academy are not ready to play in the first team. Because of this, Denayer might have to return from his loan at Celtic to help City’s first team. Denayer has done well while playing for Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a clearer date on when Fraser Forster will return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper this summer. Forster had knee surgery after falling awkwardly during a 2-0 win against Burnley two weeks ago. Estimates for his return vary from four to 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a specific timeline for the England international. He believes Kelvin Davis is a good backup, but admits he might have to add more goalkeepers if Forster’s recovery takes longer.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was very angry after his team lost a close match against Birmingham City. Rotherham was in danger of being relegated (dropped to a lower league).

Birmingham City scored first in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire then scored one goal for Rotherham, bringing the score closer.

About an hour into the game, Rob Kiernan from Birmingham handled the ball with his hands while playing against Derbyshire. Derbyshire fell inside the penalty area, and Rotherham’s players asked the referee, Dean Whitestone, to award a penalty kick. The referee refused to give the penalty.

This decision made Steve Evans visibly angry. Birmingham City held on to their lead and won the

Virgil van Dijk is worried about his place in the Dutch national team. The team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they lost in the entire qualifying campaign for the last World Cup. Despite this, coach Guus Hiddink has not contacted him. Van Dijk was selected for two squads last year, but progress is often followed by setbacks. When the Dutch team was tied 1-1 with Turkey recently, Van Dijk was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf with his club teammates instead. Although he has played well for Celtic, he has not been called up to the national team.

Celtic is complaining about the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness, which will take place later this month at Hampden. The Scottish Football Association (SFA) has already been criticized by Inverness fans because the match is scheduled for 12:15 pm on Sunday, April 18. This time is before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. Now, Celtic has also spoken out about the prices. Tickets cost £23 for the North and South stands, £15 for adults in the East Stand, and £5 for concessions in the East Stand.

Paul Murray, the temporary chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday that the previous management teams are entirely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The club will be forced to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it could not find a new advisor to meet the required rules. However, Murray stated that the new board’s plans for the future will not change, and the planned investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how poorly the team started playing against Italy on Tuesday night. This was a friendly match at the Juventus Stadium in Turin, nine months after they had played each other at the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, so people expected them to do well. However, Roy Hodgson’s team struggled in the first half and deservedly lost the goal to a header by Graziano Pelle. The final score was 1-1. Rooney said that he and the other players were upset by their performance in the first half.

Dundee United’s board responded to strong criticism from two major fan groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. These groups expressed shock that 25% of the £6.3 million paid for players Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went to unnamed parties as commissions. The fan groups also challenged claims about chairman Stephen Thompson’s level of investment in the club. In response, the board defended its performance by highlighting the team’s success on the field.

Gary Locke will officially become Kilmarnock’s permanent manager on Friday. This happens exactly eight weeks after he was first asked to manage the team until the end of the season. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning, and Locke will receive a three-year contract. On Thursday, the 39-year-old praised the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of the new chairman, Jim Mann. Locke took over as caretaker manager in February, replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents are very focused on raising children who are exceptionally talented, such as 10-year-olds who enter university or 4-year-olds who can dance like Michael Jackson. Now, a new basketball star is emerging. A video that has gone viral in China shows a small boy performing impressive basketball skills that are better than many professional players. The boy, named Mai Zizhuo, is five years old. According to People's Daily Online, he has been playing basketball since he was two and a half. The video shows him making many baskets and then dribbling two basketballs at the same time while running.

Bayern Munich will not have David Alaba for the end of the season because he has a torn knee ligament. He will be out for about seven weeks. Alaba was already out for three months earlier this season due to a partial tear in his right knee. He got this new injury while playing for Austria in a 1-1 tie against Bosnia on Tuesday. The 22-year-old said he is very disappointed, but his goal is to be ready for the final games of the season. The injury happened when Emir Spahic tackled him during the match between Austria and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR has signed Dane Tilse, an experienced Australian forward from the Canberra Raiders, to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who left the team. Tilse is 6 feet 7 inches tall and weighs over 17 stone. He has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with Hull KR and will join the team once the necessary paperwork is completed, after the Raiders agreed to let him go.

Tilse is 30 years old and has played 200 games in Australia. He will work with his former Canberra teammate, Terry Campese, who is now the captain of Hull KR and recently signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month due to injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill thinks that midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though the game is only a week after the tragic death of his cousin. Darren Cole, who used to play for Rangers’ youth team, is grieving the loss of Shaun Cole, 22. Shaun was found dead on a street in Miami last weekend and is believed to have been hit by a driver who fled the scene. Shaun was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan. He was on holiday in Florida while on leave and had attended a music festival there before being found on the sidewalk with a head injury that turned out to be fatal. Mark Burchill hopes that Darren Cole will play for Livingston on Sunday.

Alan Smith says it is not true that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was riding in after his serious injury. This happened nine years ago, during Manchester United’s 1-0 loss to Liverpool in the FA Cup.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle when he tried to stop a free-kick by John Arne Riise. The game took place at Anfield in February 2006.

At the time, reports said that Liverpool fans tried to stop Smith’s trip to the hospital. They allegedly threw bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance and shook the vehicle.

Ronny Deila has confirmed that Celtic is interested in signing Danny Wilson, the captain of Hearts. As reported earlier, Celtic might offer £400,000 for the defender, who previously played for Rangers and Liverpool. Wilson has one year left on his current contract. However, Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club has no need to sell him, even though he will be out of contract at the end of the season.

Ronny Deila says Celtic will not risk their chances in the Champions League by doing another difficult pre-season travel schedule. He blames last summer’s tour of the United States, Austria, and Germany for causing a bad 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw during the qualifying round. Celtic makes a lot of money from these pre-season games and has also traveled to Australia and the Far East in recent years. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton walked off the field after losing to Legia Warsaw. A trip to America this July has not been ruled out yet.

Franck Ribery says that reports claiming Kevin de Bruyne might replace him or Arjen Robben at Bayern Munich are false. De Bruyne played mostly on loan at Chelsea for two years before joining Wolfsburg, which is currently second in the league. This season, he has scored nine goals and leads the league in assists with 16, which is seven more than the next best player. However, Ribery argues that the 23-year-old Belgian is not the right type of player for Pep Guardiola’s team because his skills are different from Ribery’s and Robben’s.

Kelsi Langley, the girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player, has taken back her claim that he abused her. She says that her mood swings caused her to lie about being attacked.

Davon Durant, a football player at ASU, was arrested for domestic violence after Langley said he hit her in the face and grabbed her neck during an argument in his car on March 7. Because of this arrest, Durant has been suspended from the team for an unknown amount of time and might be kicked out of the university. Durant was a highly rated recruit who transferred from a college in Kansas.

It is very exciting to meet your favorite sports player. Imagine meeting them at a Starbucks while wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your photo posted on their Instagram. A young boy was lucky enough to meet Justin Verlander, a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, in this special situation. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back.

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games for Chelsea might have made him too tired to play well. He was taken off the field just 62 minutes into Belgium’s win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard has played 48 games this season for his club and his country, missing only five games for Chelsea. He played in every match for Chelsea as they won the Premier League title. However, during Belgium’s difficult 1-0 win over Israel in the European Championship qualifying, manager Marc Wilmots took Hazard off with 28 minutes left. Hazard had trouble getting past his opponent, Orel Dgani.

Police in the Northern Territory found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb. The officers noticed a strange smell, so they used an X-ray machine to look inside the meat. The X-ray showed the bag of drugs. The lamb was being shipped to a company at Darwin Airport, and was likely going to be sent to the Tiwi Islands, which are 100 kilometers north.

Former football player Clarke Carlisle says he has separated from his wife, Gemma. They were married for 14 years and lived in Yorkshire. Carlisle is struggling with depression after a suicide attempt in December. This happened two days after he was arrested for suspected drunk driving. He has moved out of the house they shared.

Paul Merson, a famous former player for Arsenal, admitted he was wrong to criticize Andros Townsend’s selection for the England team. On Tuesday night, Townsend came off the bench and scored a great goal to tie the match 1-1 against Italy in Turin. This result proved Merson’s earlier comment was incorrect. Merson had previously written in a Sky Sports article that if Townsend could make the England squad, then anyone could. After scoring, Townsend celebrated with his teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

It is common for Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas to play poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players in Holland’s 2-0 win over Spain on Tuesday. The 27-year-old said he was happy living in southwest London earlier this week, but his performance has dropped significantly. At Christmas, he looked like he would break the Barclays Premier League record for assists.

West Midlands Police arrested six people in Dover this morning for suspected terrorism related to Syria. The arrests happened around 8 a.m. in the departure area of the port.

Five of the people are men and one is a woman. Four of the men are in their 20s and live in Birmingham. The other two people—a 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman—do not have a fixed home.

All six people are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Today, people are most likely to buy treats at 12:52 pm. A study shows that Britons spend an average of £62 a week on rewards. These rewards can be small things, like a bar of chocolate or a glass of wine, or bigger things, like designer clothes and shoes. The research was done by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. Surprisingly, men spend one-third more per month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is highly respected and clearly very smart. Sometimes, you agree with what he says because it sounds correct, but when you look closer, you realize it lacks solid proof. This usually happens when he talks about Arsenal’s defense, which is actually statistically very good after their recent poor performance. Last week, however, he spoke about quotas. Specifically, he discussed FA chairman Greg Dyke’s plan to increase the number of homegrown players in a 25-player Premier League squad from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin says that his friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, but Barton later realized his mistake. After that, the two became good friends. Austin had a memorable first season in the Premier League, scoring 15 goals. People think he might play for England in the future. Everyone knows that Austin and Barton, who is the team captain, are close friends. However, their first meeting was something Austin will never forget.

This dog is his owner’s best friend because he saved him from a cold, muddy grave. The black dog was filmed helping his owner at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The video shows the man being pulled to shore by firefighters after spending nearly two hours in water that was near freezing (zero degrees Celsius). He got stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to retrieve some duck hunting gear. Fortunately, he had a cell phone and called 911. However, firefighters could not send a boat to him because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he does not expect the fans to fully support him until he wins a championship title. He joined Juventus last summer, several months after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done a great job, leading the team to a strong position in the race for the league title. Allegri replaced Antonio Conte last summer. On Saturday, Juventus will play Empoli at home, hoping to win three more points. Allegri is currently managing the team from the sidelines, and Juventus is at the top of the league.

Nathan Redmond scored the winning goal just six minutes after coming onto the field. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to Redmond along the right side of the field. Redmond ran faster than Joe Bennett and sent a low cross into the goal. Bradley Johnson scored the goal at the back of the net. This was the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

In Celoron, New York, people are upset about a statue of Lucille Ball, who is famous for being from this town. The statue has been there for six years, but locals have been angry about it since 2009. The statue’s face looks very different from how people remember the comedian, which has shocked and upset many residents. Because the statue looks so bad, a Facebook page called “We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue” has gotten more than 600 likes. Some people even call the statue “monstrous.” The statue is based on a famous scene from her TV show “I Love Lucy,” where she tries to sell a health drink while drunk.

South Sydney rugby player Issac Luke, 27, is facing accusations of being homophobic. This happened after he posted an offensive comment on social media in response to criticism from fans of the Canterbury Bulldogs.

On Saturday, Luke posted a sincere message on his official Instagram account. He was trying to find a young South Sydney fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. Luke wanted to give the boy a jersey before the Easter holiday as a way to make up for the incident, which left the boy hospitalized.

People who are afraid of spiders should be careful, because this story is scary. A man in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, was surprised when a large huntsman spider came out from inside his car door handle.

The video shows the man walking up to his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repellent on the door. This spray forced the spider to come out from under the door handle. The man calmly told the spider to leave. However, when the hairy spider’s legs appeared, the man became scared and jumped back in fear.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino says Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. Pochettino also promised he will help Kane if things do not go well.

Kane scored on his first game for England. He came on as a substitute against Lithuania at Wembley on Friday night. He scored just 79 seconds after entering the game. This goal put him within two goals of reaching 30 goals for the season.

England manager Roy Hodgson wants to keep expectations low for Kane. Kane has risen quickly in his career. He finally made it into Tottenham’s main team after spending time on loan at Leicester and Norwich.

Michael McIndoe, a former football player for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, ran a £30 million investment scheme. He promised other footballers a 20% return on their money. The scheme failed because of large debts, and McIndoe went bankrupt last October with over £2 million in debt. He used to live like a millionaire in Marbella, partying with glamorous women, but now he is surviving on handouts and being chased by creditors through the courts.

Pavel Nedved, a director at Juventus, said that Barcelona wants to sign Paul Pogba. However, Nedved stated that Pogba will not leave Juventus. He also mentioned that he was happy because Juventus did not play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

James Oliver, 48, was hit by a car driven by his girlfriend, Linda Currier, 53. Police say this happened in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night.

Currier allegedly ran over Oliver after she caught him trying to sexually abuse a 12-year-old girl. The two had argued inside the house before the incident. Oliver was left with a serious leg injury.

Liverpool wants to sign Neto, but they face strong competition from Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and several Spanish clubs. This is according to Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna.

Neto is 25 years old and his contract with Fiorentina ends in June. Liverpool was interested in signing him earlier this season because their regular goalkeeper, Simon Mignolet, was removed from the team. However, a deal in January did not happen. Now, it seems certain that Neto will leave Fiorentina in the summer.

A video on YouTube shows a Porsche Cayman crashing on Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car speeds away from a green light, swerves wildly, and hits a concrete barrier. One wheel comes off before the car stops. The video’s uploader, Richard Stewart, says that owning an expensive car does not make someone a good driver. He warns people not to let their children drive their Porsches.

Before this weekend's Premier League games, Sportsmail will give you all the details for every match, including team updates, possible player lists, betting odds, and statistics. Here is the information for Sunderland's home game against Newcastle.

Sunderland vs Newcastle United (Stadium of Light)

Team News: Sunderland

Sunderland midfielder Lee Cattermole will start the game against Newcastle on Sunday. Head coach Dick Advocaat confirmed that Cattermole is back after serving a two-game ban for getting 10 yellow cards this season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters tournament, he will become the first golfer to win every major championship. This would finish a lifelong journey for the world’s best player. With help from his sponsor, Bose, McIlroy released a video showing his path from playing on small courses as a child to becoming a top golfer, including some difficult times. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, with the text "Six weeks to Georgia" on the screen. It also includes an interview with McIlroy when he was young, before he became famous.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week's Shell Houston Open, even though the Masters tournament is coming soon. For weeks, the main topics have been Rory McIlroy trying to win his third major in a row to complete his career grand slam, and whether Tiger Woods will return to the game after staying away for a while. Although the Golf Club of Houston is set up to try to copy some of the conditions players will face at Augusta, Garcia is concentrating on ending his long wait for a win. Sergio Garcia lines up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a 31-year-old Iraq war veteran, was sentenced to 16 months in prison for stealing £17,000 from the football club where he volunteered as secretary. He took the money from Tidworth Town Football Club’s accounts by claiming he was paying rent to the landlord, even though the club was getting the building for free. Hughes used the stolen funds for personal expenses, including camping gear and a stag party in Las Vegas.

Johnny Sexton is used to being successful. Winning awards has become a regular part of his life, and he wants to keep doing it. Before playing a big match against Saracens in Paris, he talked about his success. He said he has been lucky to play for strong teams like Leinster and Ireland, and he has won trophies almost every year. The only year he did not win major awards was 2010, when he was 29 years old.

Mustafa Kamal quit as president of the International Cricket Council (ICC) on Wednesday. He said that India used its power within the ICC to change the result of the quarter-final match between India and Bangladesh.

Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, made these comments at the airport after returning from the tournament in Australia. He said, "Everyone saw what happened in the Bangladesh-India match. India used its position in the ICC to influence the outcome. From now on, I am no longer the ICC president. I would have done the same thing if it happened to any other country."

A photo shows Mustafa Kamal holding the Cricket World Cup trophy.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce supports Nigel Pearson, the manager of Leicester City. Allardyce respects Pearson for being independent and doing things his own way. The two men worked together in 2007 when Allardyce was the manager of Newcastle United. They will work together again when West Ham plays Leicester at the King Power Stadium on Saturday.

This season, Pearson has been involved in several controversial events. These include grabbing Crystal Palace player James McArthur by the throat and losing his temper with a reporter during a press conference.

Sunderland manager John O'Shea says his team must control their own destiny by beating Newcastle for the fifth time in a row. The two teams play at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Sunderland has won the last four games against Newcastle, but they really need three points to stay safe in the Premier League. If Burnley beats Tottenham in the earlier game, Sunderland could drop into the bottom three teams (the relegation zone). This makes winning against Newcastle very important.

Stoke City manager Mark Hughes believes it is time for his team to stop losing to Chelsea. Since moving up to the Premier League in 2008, Stoke has played Chelsea away eight times in all competitions and lost every single time. The last time Stoke won at Chelsea’s stadium was in 1995, when they won a League Cup match. Since a tie in 1984, Stoke has not earned any points in games at Chelsea’s home ground. Mark Hughes says his team needs to end this losing streak. In their most recent visit, Chelsea beat Stoke 3-0, and Frank Lampard celebrated the victory.

Newcastle wants to avoid losing their third game in a row when they play their rivals, Sunderland, this Sunday. They have been struggling recently because their striker, Papiss Cisse, is banned.

Newcastle is near the bottom of the league, just one point above the teams that will be relegated. However, if Cisse were not playing, Sunderland would actually be two points ahead of Newcastle in the relegation zone.

Cisse is Newcastle’s best scorer this season with 11 goals. Ten of those goals were crucial in helping Newcastle win games.

Dick Advocaat is bringing Lee Cattermole back to the center of his Sunderland team. He hopes this will help the team survive in the league. Advocaat is trying to win his fifth derby game in a row.

Cattermole is 27 years old. He missed the last two games because he was suspended. He had received 10 yellow cards during the season. Because he was suspended, he could not play in Advocaat’s first game, which was a 1-0 loss to West Ham on March 21.

Ronny Deila knows that winning a spot in the Champions League isn’t just about money. However, there is a very strong financial reason for him to lead Celtic to win their fourth title in a row: £16 million.

This week, UEFA announced how much money teams will earn in European competitions over the next three years. When Celtic last played in the Champions League group stage (in 2013–14), they played against AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona. They won one game and earned £12.6 million.
